newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch mull informal EMU "ins" group.
newsitem.headline: Dutch mull informal EMU "ins" group.

text.p: The Netherlands, currently holding the European Union (EU) presidency, said on Thursday it was considering setting up an informal council where EU finance ministers would specifically discuss the euro, the 15-member bloc's proposed new single currency.
Dutch Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm floated the idea at a dinner with his French counterpart Jean Arthuis, a ministry spokesman said from The Hague.
The informal "Stability and Growth" council would bring together finance ministers from those member states leading the way on Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
Candidates meeting strict qualification criteria for EMU's planned 1999 euro launch are expected to be selected early next year.
They would meet as a kind of super sub-committee to the regular Economic and Financial (ECOFIN) council, which discusses economic issues at an EU level.
"It's planned as a more informal ECOFIN sub-committee formed by the (EMU) "ins,'" the spokesman said, adding that the new council would not begin meeting until the "ins" had been selected in 1998.
"At this stage, it's just a tentative suggestion. It will be up to ECOFIN to decide whether it should happen."

The move is seen as something of a compromise to France, which has called for a political counter-balance to what is planned to be an independent European Central Bank (ECB) running the bloc's economic policy.
The Germans, backed by the Dutch, are keen to safeguard the ECB's independence from political interference which they believe could possibly weaken the planned single currency.
The new council would give ministers an informal forum to discuss monetary issues -- such as exchange rates between the euro, dollar and yen -- at a political level.
"The ECB will remain independent. This would be purely an informal meeting," Zalm was quoted as saying.
